title: Yellowed Mexican Cod Churros
description: A briny and molten Mexican dish featuring cod in a cozy churro form, inspired by the flavors of Chiapan cuisine, suitable for a Buddhist temple gathering.
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, cornstarch, and spices to make the churro dough.
In a separate bowl, whisk together the eggs, milk, and vegetable oil to make the wet ingredients.
Add the wet ingredients to the dry ingredients and mix until a smooth dough forms.
Cut the cod fillets into small pieces and add them to the dough, mixing until they are evenly distributed.
Heat the oil in a deep frying pan to 375 degrees Fahrenheit.
Using a piping bag or a plastic bag with a corner cut off, pipe the dough into long, thin strips.
Fry the churros in batches until they are golden brown and cooked through, about 3-4 minutes per side.
Drain the churros on paper towels and serve hot with your favorite dipping sauce.
Steam the churros for an additional 2-3 minutes to add moisture and coziness to the dish.
Serve the Yellowed Mexican Cod Churros immediately, garnished with chopped cilantro or scallions if desired.
